findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_verticals, get_public_catalog, fetch · Private data: search, fetch, answer_question, answer_question_in_card, my_matches, my_scorecard_status, my_clients, propose_scores, submit_proposal_package, list_lead_documents · Public sink: request_assessment_submit, submit_proposal_package.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_verticals, get_public_catalog, fetch · Private data: search, fetch, answer_question, answer_question_in_card, my_matches, my_scorecard_status, my_clients, propose_scores, submit_proposal_package, list_lead_documents · Public sink: request_assessment_submit, submit_proposal_package

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_public_catalog" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
